title: Derived stalk comparison for a coherent sheaf and a bounded-below complex
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], let $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] have cohomology zero in every sufficiently negative degree, and let $x\in X$. Write $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, and compute stalk complexes by applying the exact stalk functor termwise [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. The canonical comparison is an isomorphism in $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]: $$\bigl(R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F[0],E)\bigr)_x\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_A(\mathcal F_x[0],E_x).$$ Both derived internal Hom functors are [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], on the Zariski ringed site and on the one-object ringed site respectively. The comparison is natural in $\mathcal F$ and $E$, in particular it intertwines precomposition by every endomorphism of $\mathcal F$.

source.place: Tag 0GM8 (lemma-stalk-internal-hom), case (2); coherent degree-zero modules on Noetherian schemes are pseudo-coherent (perfect.tex Tag 08E8, lemma-identify-pseudo-coherent-noetherian).

proof.text: Choose $a\in\mathbf Z$ with $H^i(E)=0$ for $i<a$. For any representative $C^\bullet$ of $E$, its good truncation $G^\bullet=\tau_{\ge a}C^\bullet$ is zero below $a$ and $C^\bullet\to G^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism: in retained degrees its cohomology is that of $C^\bullet$, and the discarded cohomology is zero. Thus we may compute with a termwise bounded-below complex, without imposing quasi-coherence on $E$.

source.place: Good truncation used in the bounded-below case of lemma-stalk-internal-hom (Tag 0GM8); truncation formula in derived-categories.tex.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-coherent-affine-free-resolution] to $X,\mathcal F,x$. Obtain an affine open $U\ni x$ and a bounded-above finite-free complex $P^\bullet\to\mathcal F|_U[0]$ which is a quasi-isomorphism; choose $b$ with $P^p=0$ for $p>b$. By [lem-sc-derived-internal-hom-restrict-open] the restriction of the global derived Hom is the derived Hom of the restricted arguments. Stalks at $x$ are unchanged by this restriction: neighbourhoods contained in $U$ are cofinal among all neighbourhoods of $x$. It therefore suffices to compute on $U$.

source.place: Tag 0GM8(2), local finite-free calculation; restriction is Tag 08DL (lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U).

proof.text: [lem-sc-derived-hom-finite-free-model] identifies $H^\bullet=\mathcal Hom^\bullet_{\mathcal O_U}(P^\bullet,G^\bullet|_U)$ with a representative of $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal F|_U[0],E|_U)$. Its hypotheses hold: $P^\bullet$ is bounded above and finite free, $G^\bullet|_U$ is termwise bounded below, and the augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. Exactness of stalks [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] makes $P_x^\bullet\to\mathcal F_x[0]$ a quasi-isomorphism, with finite-free terms, and $G_x^\bullet$ represents $E_x$ and is zero below $a$. Apply the same finite-free-model lemma to the one-point ringed space with ring $A$ to compute $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(\mathcal F_x[0],E_x)$ by $\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(P_x^\bullet,G_x^\bullet)$.

source.place: Tag 0GM8(2), computation of both sides by finite-free Hom complexes; modules.tex Tag 01AG (lemma-abelian).

proof.text: In degree $n$ the Hom complex of [def-pur-hom-complex] has factors $\mathcal Hom(P^p,G^{p+n}|_U)$ only for $a-n\le p\le b$, a finite interval. For $P^p\cong\mathcal O_U^{r_p}$ the canonical germ-of-map homomorphism is the identity on $(G_x^{p+n})^{r_p}$, hence $\mathcal Hom(P^p,G^{p+n}|_U)_x\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(P_x^p,G_x^{p+n})$. Finite products commute with stalks: representatives for finitely many germs can be restricted to their common neighbourhood, and finitely many equalities of germs can be imposed on another common neighbourhood. Thus these maps give a degreewise isomorphism $\gamma:(H^\bullet)_x\to\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(P_x^\bullet,G_x^\bullet)$. The differential formula $d(f)^p=d_G^{p+n}f^p-(-1)^nf^{p+1}d_P^p$ commutes with taking germs, so $\gamma$ is an isomorphism of complexes.

source.place: Tag 0GM8(2), expanded finite-products calculation; Hom differential from section-hom-complexes.

proof.text: In the derived category, the canonical stalk comparison is the map induced by taking the germ of a local Hom and then deriving. Computing it with the finite-free model gives precisely $Q(\gamma)$: the replacement maps in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] are inverted, and germ evaluation commutes with their precomposition and postcomposition. Consequently the two models in Step 3 and the complex isomorphism in Step 4 identify the canonical comparison itself as an isomorphism in $D(A)$, rather than merely identify the cohomology groups. The same equality $(v\circ f\circ u)_x=v_x\circ f_x\circ u_x$ shows naturality in both arguments before localization; the derived functor and independence of representatives in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] preserve these commuting squares. In particular for an endomorphism $u$ of $\mathcal F$ the square is $\gamma\circ(u^*)_x=(u_x)^*\circ\gamma$.
